spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od8m6p2t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Students, Capacity, MaxLease, MaxClock

VARIABLES reservations, free, expiry, clock

vars == <<reservations, free, expiry, clock>>

\* reservations[s] = 1 means student s currently holds a seat under a lease.
\* expiry[s] is the clock tick at which s's current lease lapses if not renewed.
\* free tracks unallocated seats directly; every action that grants or
\* reclaims a seat must move exactly one unit between "held" and "free".

Held == {s \in Students : reservations[s] = 1}

Init ==
  /\ reservations = [s \in Students |-> 0]
  /\ free = Capacity
  /\ expiry = [s \in Students |-> 0]
  /\ clock = 0

Reserve(s) ==
  /\ reservations[s] = 0
  /\ free > 0
  /\ reservations' = [reservations EXCEPT ![s] = 1]
  /\ free' = free - 1
  /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![s] = clock + MaxLease]
  /\ UNCHANGED clock

Renew(s) ==
  /\ reservations[s] = 1
  /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![s] = clock + MaxLease]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reservations, free, clock>>

ExpireLease(s) ==
  /\ reservations[s] = 1
  /\ clock >= expiry[s]
  /\ reservations' = [reservations EXCEPT ![s] = 0]
  /\ free' = free + 1
  /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![s] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED clock

Release(s) ==
  /\ reservations[s] = 1
  /\ reservations' = [reservations EXCEPT ![s] = 0]
  /\ free' = free + 1
  /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![s] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED clock

\* The admin override bypasses the expiry check but still just relocates a
\* held seat from one student to another, so it cannot inflate capacity.
AdminReassign(s1, s2) ==
  /\ s1 # s2
  /\ reservations[s1] = 1
  /\ reservations[s2] = 0
  /\ reservations' = [reservations EXCEPT ![s1] = 0, ![s2] = 1]
  /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![s1] = 0, ![s2] = clock + MaxLease]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<free, clock>>

Tick ==
  /\ clock < MaxClock
  /\ clock' = clock + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reservations, free, expiry>>

Next ==
  \/ \E s \in Students : Reserve(s)
  \/ \E s \in Students : Renew(s)
  \/ \E s \in Students : ExpireLease(s)
  \/ \E s \in Students : Release(s)
  \/ \E s1 \in Students, s2 \in Students : AdminReassign(s1, s2)
  \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Core conservation claim: held seats plus free seats always equal capacity,
\* across every ordinary action and across the admin override alike.
SeatsConserved == Cardinality(Held) + free = Capacity

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Students = {s1, s2, s3}
  Capacity = 3
  MaxLease = 2
  MaxClock = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT SeatsConserved
nl: A university course-registration system manages a fixed pool of seats in a single course section. A student may reserve a free seat, which grants a time-bounded lease that must later be renewed or it will lapse. A student holding a seat may renew the lease before it expires, or may voluntarily release the seat early, in both cases keeping the seat accounting consistent with the section's fixed capacity. When a global clock advances past a held seat's expiry time and the student has not renewed, the registration system automatically reclaims that seat back into the free pool. A privileged registrar may also invoke an admin override that reassigns a seat directly from one currently-enrolled student to another currently-unenrolled student, bypassing the normal expiry wait, but the override still only moves an already-allocated seat between two students rather than creating or discarding capacity. The full action set is: Reserve, Renew, ExpireLease, Release, AdminReassign, and Tick (advancing the shared clock). SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state the number of seats currently held by students plus the number of seats currently free equals the section's fixed capacity.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od16m8p1t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Instances, Records, None, MaxVersion

ASSUME None \notin Instances

\* Two dispenser instances share one lock pool over the record set.
\* coarseLock gates which instance may even approach a slot; fineLock is the
\* inner lock that must be held across a whole read-modify-write hand-off.
\* cache remembers the version an instance last read, per record, so we can
\* tell whether a pending write would be based on a stale snapshot.

VARIABLES coarseLock, fineLock, version, value, cache

vars == <<coarseLock, fineLock, version, value, cache>>

Init ==
    /\ coarseLock = [r \in Records |-> None]
    /\ fineLock = [r \in Records |-> None]
    /\ version = [r \in Records |-> 0]
    /\ value = [r \in Records |-> 0]
    /\ cache = [i \in Instances |-> [r \in Records |-> None]]

AcquireCoarse(i, r) ==
    /\ coarseLock[r] = None
    /\ coarseLock' = [coarseLock EXCEPT ![r] = i]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fineLock, version, value, cache>>

AcquireFine(i, r) ==
    /\ coarseLock[r] = i
    /\ fineLock[r] = None
    /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT ![r] = i]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, version, value, cache>>

ReadRecord(i, r) ==
    /\ fineLock[r] = i
    /\ cache[i][r] = None
    /\ cache' = [cache EXCEPT ![i][r] = version[r]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, fineLock, version, value>>

\* A write is only legal while the fine lock is still held, so no other
\* instance could have advanced version[r] since the cached read happened.
WriteRecord(i, r) ==
    /\ fineLock[r] = i
    /\ cache[i][r] # None
    /\ version[r] < MaxVersion
    /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![r] = @ + 1]
    /\ value' = [value EXCEPT ![r] = @ + 1]
    /\ cache' = [cache EXCEPT ![i][r] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, fineLock>>

\* A pharmacist may also decide not to dispense after reading (e.g. the
\* prescription is already fulfilled); this drops the cache without a write
\* so the fine lock can still be released once version hits MaxVersion.
AbandonRead(i, r) ==
    /\ fineLock[r] = i
    /\ cache[i][r] # None
    /\ cache' = [cache EXCEPT ![i][r] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, fineLock, version, value>>

ReleaseLocks(i, r) ==
    /\ fineLock[r] = i
    /\ cache[i][r] = None
    /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT ![r] = None]
    /\ coarseLock' = [coarseLock EXCEPT ![r] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, value, cache>>

Next ==
    \E i \in Instances, r \in Records :
        \/ AcquireCoarse(i, r)
        \/ AcquireFine(i, r)
        \/ ReadRecord(i, r)
        \/ WriteRecord(i, r)
        \/ AbandonRead(i, r)
        \/ ReleaseLocks(i, r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No lost updates: any instance still nursing a cached read must still hold
\* the fine lock, and that cache must still agree with the live version -
\* i.e. nobody could have overwritten the record out from under it.
NoLostUpdate ==
    \A i \in Instances, r \in Records :
        cache[i][r] # None => (fineLock[r] = i /\ cache[i][r] = version[r])

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    i1 = i1
    i2 = i2
    r1 = r1
    r2 = r2
    NoneVal = NoneVal
    Instances = {i1, i2}
    Records = {r1, r2}
    None = NoneVal
    MaxVersion = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A pharmacy operates two independent dispenser instances that both draw from one shared pool of prescription records. Each record carries a version counter and a quantity value that dispensers must update without silently overwriting a concurrent change made by the other instance. To touch a record, a dispenser instance first acquires a coarse, pool-level lock on the record's slot, then must additionally acquire a fine-grained lock before it is allowed to read or modify the record's contents. Once holding the fine lock, an instance reads the record's current version into a private cache, then either applies its dispensing update (which advances the version and quantity together) or abandons the cached read if no dispense is needed, and finally releases the fine lock followed by the coarse lock. Because both instances draw from the very same underlying lock pool, the fine lock is the only thing standing between a stale cached read and an update that clobbers someone else's concurrent write. The full action set is: AcquireCoarse, AcquireFine, ReadRecord, WriteRecord, AbandonRead, and ReleaseLocks.
SAFETY PROPERTY: A dispenser instance holding a cached read of a prescription record can only carry that cache forward while it still holds the record's fine lock and the cached version still matches the record's live version, so neither instance ever commits a dispensing update built on a stale, overwritten read of the shared record.

spec_text:
------------------------- MODULE W4Od3m0p2t3 -------------------------
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Banks, Hub, InitBalance, Amount, SlowBank, MaxDelay

ASSUME /\ Hub \notin Banks
       /\ SlowBank \in Banks
       /\ InitBalance \in Nat
       /\ Amount \in Nat /\ Amount <= InitBalance
       /\ MaxDelay \in Nat

Accounts == Banks \cup {Hub}

VARIABLES balance, version, phase, snap, slowDelay

vars == <<balance, version, phase, snap, slowDelay>>

\* Each account (bank or hub) has a version stamp bumped on every write.
\* A bank commits its transfer only if the versions it read still hold at
\* commit time (optimistic locking); otherwise it discards the read and retries.
\* slowDelay models a bank that is merely slow, never failed: it must still
\* eventually reach zero and commit, just after extra internal ticks.

Init ==
  /\ balance = [a \in Accounts |-> IF a = Hub THEN 0 ELSE InitBalance]
  /\ version = [a \in Accounts |-> 0]
  /\ phase = [b \in Banks |-> "idle"]
  /\ snap = [b \in Banks |-> [ownV |-> 0, hubV |-> 0]]
  /\ slowDelay = MaxDelay

ReadSnapshot(b) ==
  /\ phase[b] = "idle"
  /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![b] = [ownV |-> version[b], hubV |-> version[Hub]]]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![b] = "snapped"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<balance, version, slowDelay>>

CommitTransfer(b) ==
  /\ phase[b] = "snapped"
  /\ snap[b].ownV = version[b]
  /\ snap[b].hubV = version[Hub]
  /\ (b # SlowBank \/ slowDelay = 0)
  /\ balance' = [balance EXCEPT ![b] = @ - Amount, ![Hub] = @ + Amount]
  /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![b] = @ + 1, ![Hub] = @ + 1]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![b] = "committed"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, slowDelay>>

RetryOnConflict(b) ==
  /\ phase[b] = "snapped"
  /\ \/ snap[b].ownV # version[b]
     \/ snap[b].hubV # version[Hub]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![b] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<balance, version, snap, slowDelay>>

DelayTick ==
  /\ phase[SlowBank] = "snapped"
  /\ slowDelay > 0
  /\ slowDelay' = slowDelay - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<balance, version, phase, snap>>

Next ==
  \/ \E b \in Banks : ReadSnapshot(b)
  \/ \E b \in Banks : CommitTransfer(b)
  \/ \E b \in Banks : RetryOnConflict(b)
  \/ DelayTick

Fairness ==
  /\ \A b \in Banks : WF_vars(ReadSnapshot(b))
  /\ \A b \in Banks : WF_vars(CommitTransfer(b))
  /\ \A b \in Banks : WF_vars(RetryOnConflict(b))
  /\ WF_vars(DelayTick)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ Fairness

RECURSIVE SumBal(_)
SumBal(S) == IF S = {} THEN 0
             ELSE LET x == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE
                  IN balance[x] + SumBal(S \ {x})

\* Conservation: nothing is created or destroyed by a commit or a retry --
\* the pool of money is just shuffled between banks and the hub.
Conservation == balance[Hub] + SumBal(Banks) = Cardinality(Banks) * InitBalance

AllSettle == \A b \in Banks : <>(phase[b] = "committed")

=======================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Banks = {b1, b2, b3}
  Hub = h
  InitBalance = 30
  Amount = 10
  SlowBank = b1
  MaxDelay = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT Conservation

PROPERTY AllSettle

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A set of banks take part in an interbank settlement batch that nets their positions into a shared clearing hub account. Every ledger row -- each bank's own account and the hub account -- carries a version counter that is bumped whenever its balance changes. To settle, a bank first takes a snapshot of its own account's version and the hub's version (ReadSnapshot), then tries to commit its transfer only if both versions still match what it read (CommitTransfer), debiting itself and crediting the hub atomically while incrementing both versions. If some other bank's settlement bumped the hub's version between the snapshot and the attempt, the compare-and-swap fails, the bank throws away its stale snapshot, and it starts over from scratch (RetryOnConflict). One designated bank is known to run slow: even once its snapshot is valid, its internal processing needs a bounded number of extra delay ticks (DelayTick) before it is allowed to commit, but it is never treated as failed and keeps making progress toward its own commit. Because commits are atomic debit-and-credit pairs against the hub, no money is ever created or destroyed by a retry, however many times it happens.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the sum of every bank's balance plus the hub's balance always equals the total of all banks' initial balances, at every reachable state including mid-retry.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every bank's settlement transfer, including the slow bank's, eventually commits.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od6m5p5t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets, Sequences

CONSTANTS Cars, NoCar, MinCap, MaxCap

ASSUME /\ NoCar \notin Cars
       /\ MinCap \in Nat /\ MaxCap \in Nat
       /\ 1 <= MinCap /\ MinCap <= MaxCap
       /\ MaxCap = Cardinality(Cars)

VARIABLES active, capacity, candidate, votes, retired, log

vars == <<active, capacity, candidate, votes, retired, log>>

\* Quorum for the irreversible retirement scales with current bank capacity:
\* a smaller active fleet needs fewer votes to take one more car out of service.
QuorumSize(n) == (n \div 2) + 1

Init ==
  /\ active = Cars
  /\ capacity = MaxCap
  /\ candidate = NoCar
  /\ votes = {}
  /\ retired = {}
  /\ log = <<>>

ProposeRetire(c) ==
  /\ candidate = NoCar
  /\ c \in active
  /\ candidate' = c
  /\ votes' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<active, capacity, retired, log>>

CastVote(v) ==
  /\ candidate # NoCar
  /\ v \in active
  /\ v \notin votes
  /\ votes' = votes \cup {v}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<active, capacity, candidate, retired, log>>

\* The irreversible action itself: fires only once the votes collected for the
\* current candidate meet the quorum computed from the CURRENT capacity.
ExecuteRetire ==
  /\ candidate # NoCar
  /\ Cardinality(votes) >= QuorumSize(capacity)
  /\ retired' = retired \cup {candidate}
  /\ active' = active \ {candidate}
  /\ capacity' = capacity - 1
  /\ log' = Append(log, candidate)
  /\ candidate' = NoCar
  /\ votes' = {}

\* Facilities retarget the fleet's active size; only allowed between voting
\* rounds, so this is where the twist (capacity change) can move the quorum bar.
AdjustCapacity(n) ==
  /\ candidate = NoCar
  /\ n \in MinCap..MaxCap
  /\ n <= Cardinality(Cars \ retired)
  /\ active' \in {S \in SUBSET (Cars \ retired) : Cardinality(S) = n}
  /\ capacity' = n
  /\ UNCHANGED <<candidate, votes, retired, log>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Cars : ProposeRetire(c)
  \/ \E v \in Cars : CastVote(v)
  \/ ExecuteRetire
  \/ \E n \in MinCap..MaxCap : AdjustCapacity(n)

Fairness ==
  /\ WF_vars(\E v \in Cars : CastVote(v))
  /\ WF_vars(ExecuteRetire)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ Fairness

\* SAFETY: the append-only retirement log never records the same car twice --
\* the irreversible action really does happen at most once per car.
NoDuplicateRetirement ==
  \A i, j \in 1..Len(log) : i # j => log[i] # log[j]

\* LIVENESS: once a car is nominated it does not stall forever mid-vote --
\* the quorum mechanism, given fair voting, always drives it to retirement.
EventualCompletion == \A c \in Cars : [](candidate = c => <>(c \in retired))

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
Cars = {c1, c2, c3}
NoCar = NoCar
MinCap = 1
MaxCap = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NoDuplicateRetirement

PROPERTY EventualCompletion

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A skyscraper's elevator bank draws from a fixed pool of cars, a subset of which are active in service at any time. Retiring a car from service permanently (structural decommissioning, not a temporary maintenance pull) requires quorum approval: any active car may be nominated as the current retirement candidate, and other active cars cast votes for that candidate. Once the number of votes reaches the quorum threshold, the retirement executes, permanently logging the car as retired and shrinking the bank's operating capacity by one. Facilities can also retarget how many cars are kept in active service, choosing any count between a configured minimum and the number of cars not yet retired, but only between voting rounds so a round's threshold never shifts underneath it. Because the quorum threshold is computed from the bank's current operating capacity rather than a fixed number, growing or shrinking the active fleet directly changes how many votes the next irreversible retirement needs. The full action set is: nominate a car as retirement candidate, cast a vote for the current candidate, execute a retirement once quorum is met, and retarget operating capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no elevator car is ever recorded as permanently retired more than once in the retirement log.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every car that becomes a retirement candidate is eventually actually retired.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od2m9p5t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANT MaxEpoch

VARIABLES ctrlEpoch, robotEpoch, inbox, dropCount, issued

vars == <<ctrlEpoch, robotEpoch, inbox, dropCount, issued>>

Epochs == 0..MaxEpoch
Kinds == {"Reconf", "Drop"}
Messages == [epoch: Epochs, kind: Kinds]

\* Epoch-numbered reconfiguration: the controller bumps ctrlEpoch and
\* broadcasts a Reconf message; the robot only adopts a Reconf that
\* strictly advances its own fence, so a reordered or duplicated
\* announcement can never push the fence backward.

TypeOK ==
  /\ ctrlEpoch \in Epochs
  /\ robotEpoch \in Epochs
  /\ inbox \subseteq Messages
  /\ dropCount \in 0..2
  /\ issued \subseteq Epochs

Init ==
  /\ ctrlEpoch = 0
  /\ robotEpoch = 0
  /\ inbox = {}
  /\ dropCount = 0
  /\ issued = {}

Reconfigure ==
  /\ ctrlEpoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ ctrlEpoch' = ctrlEpoch + 1
  /\ inbox' = inbox \cup {[epoch |-> ctrlEpoch + 1, kind |-> "Reconf"]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<robotEpoch, dropCount, issued>>

IssueDropCmd ==
  /\ dropCount = 0
  /\ ctrlEpoch \notin issued
  /\ inbox' = inbox \cup {[epoch |-> ctrlEpoch, kind |-> "Drop"]}
  /\ issued' = issued \cup {ctrlEpoch}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ctrlEpoch, robotEpoch, dropCount>>

\* Messages are never removed from inbox on delivery, so any message can
\* be redelivered later -- this models reordering, delay and duplication
\* all at once: delivery order is fully nondeterministic.
DeliverReconf ==
  \E m \in inbox :
    /\ m.kind = "Reconf"
    /\ m.epoch > robotEpoch
    /\ robotEpoch' = m.epoch
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ctrlEpoch, inbox, dropCount, issued>>

\* The epoch fence: a Drop is honored only when its tag matches the
\* robot's current fence AND the pallet has not already been dropped.
\* A stale (old-epoch) or duplicate Drop message is simply never
\* matched and so can never re-trigger the irreversible action.
DeliverDrop ==
  \E m \in inbox :
    /\ m.kind = "Drop"
    /\ m.epoch = robotEpoch
    /\ dropCount = 0
    /\ dropCount' = dropCount + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ctrlEpoch, robotEpoch, inbox, issued>>

Next == Reconfigure \/ IssueDropCmd \/ DeliverReconf \/ DeliverDrop

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Safety: the irreversible pallet-drop fires at most once, even though
\* Reconf/Drop messages can be delivered out of order, late, or twice.
DropAtMostOnce == dropCount <= 1

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  MaxEpoch = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT DropAtMostOnce

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A fleet controller manages a single warehouse robot tasked with dropping a pallet into a delivery bay, an action that cannot be undone once performed. The controller periodically reconfigures the system by advancing a monotonically increasing epoch number and broadcasting the new epoch to the robot as a Reconf message. Once it decides the drop is warranted for the current epoch, the controller sends a Drop command tagged with that same epoch number. The underlying network can reorder, delay, or duplicate any in-flight message, so the robot may receive its Reconf and Drop messages in any order and may see the same message more than once. The robot only advances its local epoch fence when it receives a Reconf message whose epoch is strictly greater than its current fence, so the fence can never move backward even under reordering. The robot performs the pallet drop only when a delivered Drop message's epoch exactly matches its current fence and the drop has not already occurred. The full action set is: the controller advancing its epoch and announcing it (Reconfigure), the controller issuing a fenced Drop command for the current epoch (IssueDropCmd), the robot adopting a newer epoch from a delivered Reconf message (DeliverReconf), and the robot executing the drop upon a matching, non-stale Drop message (DeliverDrop).
SAFETY PROPERTY: The pallet drop action executes at most once, no matter how controller-to-robot messages are reordered, delayed, or duplicated.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od10m2p4t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Trains, NumBlocks, Cap

ASSUME NumBlocks \in Nat \ {0}
ASSUME Cap \in Nat \ {0}
ASSUME Cardinality(Trains) <= NumBlocks

Blocks == 1 .. NumBlocks
Succ(b) == IF b = NumBlocks THEN 1 ELSE b + 1

VARIABLES pos, tstate, vote, dest

vars == <<pos, tstate, vote, dest>>

\* Two-phase commit per train: the current block is the coordinator, the
\* destination block's controller is the sole participant. A "yes" vote
\* reserves a capacity slot immediately; commit only converts that
\* reservation into physical occupancy, it never adds a fresh unit of load.

InitBlock == CHOOSE b \in Blocks : TRUE

\* Trains start one-per-block (an injection exists since Trains fits in
\* Blocks) so the very first state already respects capacity.
InitPos == CHOOSE f \in [Trains -> Blocks] :
              \A x, y \in Trains : x # y => f[x] # f[y]

Occupied(b) == Cardinality({t \in Trains : pos[t] = b})
Reserved(b) == Cardinality({t \in Trains :
                  /\ dest[t] = b /\ tstate[t] = "prepare" /\ vote[t] = "yes"})
Load(b) == Occupied(b) + Reserved(b)

Init ==
  /\ pos = InitPos
  /\ tstate = [t \in Trains |-> "idle"]
  /\ vote = [t \in Trains |-> "none"]
  /\ dest = InitPos

RequestMove(t) ==
  /\ tstate[t] = "idle"
  /\ dest' = [dest EXCEPT ![t] = Succ(pos[t])]
  /\ tstate' = [tstate EXCEPT ![t] = "prepare"]
  /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![t] = "pending"]
  /\ UNCHANGED pos

\* The participant may cast this vote arbitrarily many steps after the
\* prepare request -- it is slow, not failed -- but while pending, no
\* other action lets the requesting train advance.
Vote(t) ==
  /\ tstate[t] = "prepare"
  /\ vote[t] = "pending"
  /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![t] = IF Load(dest[t]) < Cap THEN "yes" ELSE "no"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pos, tstate, dest>>

Commit(t) ==
  /\ tstate[t] = "prepare"
  /\ vote[t] = "yes"
  /\ pos' = [pos EXCEPT ![t] = dest[t]]
  /\ tstate' = [tstate EXCEPT ![t] = "idle"]
  /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![t] = "none"]
  /\ dest' = [dest EXCEPT ![t] = InitBlock]

Abort(t) ==
  /\ tstate[t] = "prepare"
  /\ vote[t] = "no"
  /\ tstate' = [tstate EXCEPT ![t] = "idle"]
  /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![t] = "none"]
  /\ dest' = [dest EXCEPT ![t] = InitBlock]
  /\ UNCHANGED pos

Next == \E t \in Trains : RequestMove(t) \/ Vote(t) \/ Commit(t) \/ Abort(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* SAFETY: physical occupancy of every block stays within its declared
\* capacity, even though a slow participant may leave votes pending
\* indefinitely -- slowness blocks progress, it never bypasses the vote.
CapacityOK == \A b \in Blocks : Occupied(b) <= Cap

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT CapacityOK

CONSTANTS
  t1 = t1
  t2 = t2
  t3 = t3
  Trains = {t1, t2, t3}
  NumBlocks = 3
  Cap = 2
nl:
A subway line is divided into a small ring of signalling blocks, each guarded by its own local signalling controller and physically able to hold only a limited number of trains at once. When a train wants to advance from its current block into the next block on the ring, its controller acts as a two-phase-commit coordinator: it sends a prepare request to the destination block's controller, which is the sole participant deciding whether room exists. The participant computes the block's current load -- trains physically present plus trains already reserved via an earlier yes vote -- and answers yes only if that load is still below the block's capacity, otherwise it answers no. The coordinator may only advance the train into the block once the participant's yes vote has been received; a no vote causes the coordinator to abandon the attempt and return the train to idle so it can retry later. Crucially, the destination participant is never assumed to fail: it may simply be slow, leaving its vote pending for an arbitrary number of steps while other trains continue to request moves, vote, commit, or abort elsewhere, but a pending vote can never be treated as an implicit yes and never lets the requesting train slip into the block unauthorized. Because a yes vote reserves capacity the instant it is cast, and a commit only converts that existing reservation into physical occupancy rather than adding a fresh unit of load, no sequence of interleaved requests, slow votes, commits, and aborts can ever push a block's train count past its declared capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No signalling block ever holds more trains than its declared physical capacity, regardless of how long any participant's vote remains pending.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od10m4p1t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Blocks, SlowBlock, Cap, MaxVal, MaxEnq

ASSUME SlowBlock \in Blocks

VARIABLES queue, record, lastApplied, enqCtr, slowBusy

vars == <<queue, record, lastApplied, enqCtr, slowBusy>>

\* queue[b] is block b's bounded work queue of pending signal-state updates.
\* enqCtr/lastApplied together let NoLostUpdates check that every enqueued
\* update is accounted for exactly once, in order, never dropped or skipped.

Init ==
  /\ queue = [b \in Blocks |-> <<>>]
  /\ record = [b \in Blocks |-> 0]
  /\ lastApplied = [b \in Blocks |-> 0]
  /\ enqCtr = [b \in Blocks |-> 0]
  /\ slowBusy = FALSE

Enqueue(b, v) ==
  /\ Len(queue[b]) < Cap
  /\ enqCtr[b] < MaxEnq
  /\ queue' = [queue EXCEPT ![b] = Append(@, [val |-> v, seq |-> enqCtr[b] + 1])]
  /\ enqCtr' = [enqCtr EXCEPT ![b] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<record, lastApplied, slowBusy>>

Apply(b) ==
  /\ queue[b] # <<>>
  /\ (b = SlowBlock => ~slowBusy)
  /\ LET u == Head(queue[b]) IN
       /\ record' = [record EXCEPT ![b] = u.val]
       /\ lastApplied' = [lastApplied EXCEPT ![b] = u.seq]
       /\ queue' = [queue EXCEPT ![b] = Tail(@)]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<enqCtr, slowBusy>>

\* The slow controller may stall (get occupied) instead of servicing
\* its queue right away -- it is slow, not failed.
Stall ==
  /\ queue[SlowBlock] # <<>>
  /\ ~slowBusy
  /\ slowBusy' = TRUE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, record, lastApplied, enqCtr>>

WakeUp ==
  /\ slowBusy
  /\ slowBusy' = FALSE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, record, lastApplied, enqCtr>>

Next ==
  \/ \E b \in Blocks, v \in 1..MaxVal : Enqueue(b, v)
  \/ \E b \in Blocks : Apply(b)
  \/ Stall
  \/ WakeUp

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ SF_vars(Apply(SlowBlock))
  /\ \A b \in Blocks \ {SlowBlock} : WF_vars(Apply(b))
  /\ WF_vars(WakeUp)

\* Nothing enqueued for a block is ever lost, duplicated, or applied
\* out of sequence: applied + pending always equals total enqueued,
\* and a nonempty queue's head is always exactly the next in order.
NoLostUpdates ==
  \A b \in Blocks :
    /\ lastApplied[b] + Len(queue[b]) = enqCtr[b]
    /\ (queue[b] # <<>> => Head(queue[b]).seq = lastApplied[b] + 1)

\* Liveness: the slow controller's backlog always drains, even though
\* it may stall arbitrarily many times first.
QueueDrains == queue[SlowBlock] # <<>> ~> queue[SlowBlock] = <<>>

====

CONSTANTS
  b1 = b1
  b2 = b2
  b3 = b3
  Blocks = {b1, b2, b3}
  SlowBlock = b1
  Cap = 2
  MaxVal = 2
  MaxEnq = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NoLostUpdates

PROPERTY QueueDrains

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A subway signalling block system gives each track block its own bounded work queue that buffers pending signal-state updates (clear, caution, stop) before they are applied to that block's entry in a shared block-state record. Upstream traffic-control logic may enqueue a new update for a block only when that block's queue still has spare capacity; when the queue is full the enqueue is simply refused, so the mechanism applies backpressure instead of ever overwriting a pending update. Each block's own controller dequeues and applies updates strictly in the order they were enqueued, stamping the shared record with the update's sequence number so nothing can be skipped, duplicated, or applied out of turn. One designated block runs an older, slower controller that is allowed to stall in a busy phase before it resumes servicing its queue, but it is never treated as failed and it always eventually wakes back up. Because the slow controller can stall, its queue can temporarily pile up, but the system is built so it keeps making real progress rather than stalling forever.
SAFETY PROPERTY: for every block, applied updates plus still-queued updates always equal the total number ever enqueued for that block, and the head of any nonempty queue is always exactly the next update in sequence, so no update to the shared signal-state record is ever lost, skipped, or applied out of order.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: whenever the slow-but-live block controller's queue holds a pending update, that queue eventually becomes empty, i.e. every signal-state update enqueued for the slow controller is eventually applied.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od2m2p5t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Participants

VARIABLES decision, partState, msgsOut, msgsIn, dropCount

vars == <<decision, partState, msgsOut, msgsIn, dropCount>>

\* Two-phase commit over a warehouse robot fleet: the coordinator broadcasts
\* prepare/commit/abort over an unordered channel (msgsOut/msgsIn are sets,
\* not queues), so a robot can see a later message before an earlier one.
\* AtMostOnceDrop is the safety net: the irreversible pallet-drop fires once
\* fleet-wide only once every participant's local state has latched into
\* "committed", no matter what order the messages actually arrived in.

TypeOK ==
  /\ decision \in {"pending", "commit", "abort"}
  /\ partState \in [Participants -> {"idle", "prepared", "committed", "aborted"}]
  /\ msgsOut \subseteq (Participants \X {"prepare", "commit", "abort"})
  /\ msgsIn \subseteq (Participants \X {"yes", "no"})
  /\ dropCount \in 0..1

Init ==
  /\ decision = "pending"
  /\ partState = [p \in Participants |-> "idle"]
  /\ msgsOut = {}
  /\ msgsIn = {}
  /\ dropCount = 0

SendPrepare ==
  /\ msgsOut = {}
  /\ msgsOut' = {<<p, "prepare">> : p \in Participants}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<decision, partState, msgsIn, dropCount>>

Vote(p) ==
  /\ <<p, "prepare">> \in msgsOut
  /\ partState[p] = "idle"
  /\ \E v \in {"yes", "no"} :
       /\ partState' = [partState EXCEPT ![p] = "prepared"]
       /\ msgsIn' = msgsIn \cup {<<p, v>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<decision, msgsOut, dropCount>>

CoordinatorDecide ==
  /\ decision = "pending"
  /\ \A p \in Participants : \E v \in {"yes", "no"} : <<p, v>> \in msgsIn
  /\ LET d == IF \A p \in Participants : <<p, "yes">> \in msgsIn
              THEN "commit" ELSE "abort"
     IN /\ decision' = d
        /\ msgsOut' = msgsOut \cup {<<p, d>> : p \in Participants}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<partState, msgsIn, dropCount>>

Apply(p) ==
  /\ partState[p] = "prepared"
  /\ \/ <<p, "commit">> \in msgsOut
     \/ <<p, "abort">> \in msgsOut
  /\ partState' = [partState EXCEPT ![p] =
        IF <<p, "commit">> \in msgsOut THEN "committed" ELSE "aborted"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<decision, msgsOut, msgsIn, dropCount>>

ExecuteDrop ==
  /\ decision = "commit"
  /\ \A p \in Participants : partState[p] = "committed"
  /\ dropCount = 0
  /\ dropCount' = 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<decision, partState, msgsOut, msgsIn>>

VoteAny == \E p \in Participants : Vote(p)
ApplyAny == \E p \in Participants : Apply(p)
Idle == UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
  \/ SendPrepare
  \/ VoteAny
  \/ CoordinatorDecide
  \/ ApplyAny
  \/ ExecuteDrop
  \/ Idle

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(SendPrepare)
  /\ WF_vars(VoteAny)
  /\ WF_vars(CoordinatorDecide)
  /\ WF_vars(ApplyAny)
  /\ WF_vars(ExecuteDrop)

\* Safety: the fleet-wide irreversible pallet-drop cannot fire twice, even
\* though duplicate/reordered commit messages linger in msgsOut forever.
AtMostOnceDrop == dropCount <= 1

\* Liveness: the transaction cannot stall in "pending" forever, and once it
\* commits the drop is guaranteed to actually execute, not just get decided.
FleetProgress ==
  /\ <>(decision # "pending")
  /\ (decision = "commit") ~> (dropCount = 1)

====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Participants = {r1, r2, r3}

INVARIANT AtMostOnceDrop

PROPERTY FleetProgress
nl:
A small fleet of warehouse robots executes a single pallet-relocation transaction coordinated via two-phase commit: a coordinator broadcasts a prepare request to every participant robot, each participant locally votes yes or no on whether it can safely reposition its arm, and the coordinator broadcasts a commit or abort decision once every vote is in. All coordinator-to-participant and participant-to-coordinator messages travel over an unordered wireless channel, so a robot may observe a commit or abort message before it has processed the matching prepare, or see a stale retransmitted message long after the decision was made. Each participant's local state machine only accepts a commit/abort message once it has already recorded its own prepared state, so out-of-order or duplicated delivery cannot let a robot short-circuit the protocol. Only after every participant in the fleet has locally committed does the fleet perform the actual irreversible action: releasing the pallet onto the destination conveyor. Because that release is physically undoable, the fleet must guarantee it triggers at most once, no matter how the prepare/commit/abort messages get reordered or duplicated in transit. The full action set is: the coordinator broadcasting prepare, each participant voting yes or no on a pending prepare, the coordinator computing and broadcasting the commit/abort decision, each participant applying whichever decision message it observes, and the fleet firing the one-shot irreversible pallet release once all participants have committed.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the irreversible pallet-release action fires at most once fleet-wide, even under arbitrarily reordered or duplicated two-phase-commit messages.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every prepared pallet-relocation transaction eventually reaches a coordinator decision and never stalls in pending forever, and whenever that decision is commit, the irreversible pallet release is eventually actually executed.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od9m1p1t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS NumParticipants, MaxRequest, MaxSlow

Participants == 1..NumParticipants

\* Ring successor: the token moves around a fixed cycle of substations.
Succ(p) == IF p = NumParticipants THEN 1 ELSE p + 1

VARIABLES token, requested, committed, record, slowCount

vars == <<token, requested, committed, record, slowCount>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ token \in Participants
  /\ requested \in [Participants -> 0..MaxRequest]
  /\ committed \in [Participants -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ record \in 0..(NumParticipants * MaxRequest)
  /\ slowCount \in 0..MaxSlow

Init ==
  /\ token = 1
  /\ requested = [p \in Participants |-> 0]
  /\ committed = [p \in Participants |-> FALSE]
  /\ record = 0
  /\ slowCount = 0

\* A substation may lodge exactly one shed request, at any time, before it
\* has ever submitted one; the amount is then frozen until it is committed.
Submit(p) ==
  /\ requested[p] = 0
  /\ \E amt \in 1..MaxRequest :
       requested' = [requested EXCEPT ![p] = amt]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, committed, record, slowCount>>

\* Only the current token holder may fold its own request into the shared
\* ledger, and only once -- this is the exclusive-access write path.
Apply ==
  /\ requested[token] > 0
  /\ ~committed[token]
  /\ record' = record + requested[token]
  /\ committed' = [committed EXCEPT ![token] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, requested, slowCount>>

\* The twist: a holder can be slow -- it may delay handoff for a bounded
\* number of cycles without ever losing the token or its commit rights.
Stall ==
  /\ slowCount < MaxSlow
  /\ slowCount' = slowCount + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, requested, committed, record>>

\* A holder only relinquishes the token once its own request is either
\* absent or already committed, so a delayed handoff can never orphan
\* an uncommitted request or let two holders race on the ledger.
PassToken ==
  /\ \/ requested[token] = 0
     \/ committed[token]
  /\ token' = Succ(token)
  /\ slowCount' = 0
  /\ UNCHANGED <<requested, committed, record>>

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Participants : Submit(p)
  \/ Apply
  \/ Stall
  \/ PassToken

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

RECURSIVE SumCommitted(_)
SumCommitted(S) ==
  IF S = {} THEN 0
  ELSE LET p == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE
       IN (IF committed[p] THEN requested[p] ELSE 0) + SumCommitted(S \ {p})

\* No lost updates: the ledger total is always exactly the sum of the
\* requests that have actually been committed -- never short, never double.
NoLostUpdates == record = SumCommitted(Participants)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  NumParticipants = 3
  MaxRequest = 3
  MaxSlow = 2
INVARIANT NoLostUpdates
nl:
A regional power grid uses a ring of substations coordinating emergency load-shedding: only the substation currently holding the ring token may write into the shared cumulative shed ledger. Each substation may, before it has ever submitted, record one load-shed request of an amount up to a configured maximum; once submitted that amount is fixed and cannot be resubmitted. Whichever substation currently holds the token may commit its own outstanding request into the shared ledger, but only once, and only while it still holds the token. Because grid technicians sometimes need extra time to double-check readings before handing the token onward, a token holder may also stall, deliberately delaying handoff for a bounded number of cycles, without losing the token or its right to commit -- it is slow, never failed. A holder passes the token to its ring successor only once it has either committed its pending request or has nothing pending. The system must guarantee that the shared ledger always exactly reflects the sum of every request that has actually been committed, even when a holder lingers before releasing the token, so that no substation's committed update is ever lost, duplicated, or overwritten by a race for ledger access.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The cumulative load-shed ledger always equals exactly the sum of committed substation requests, so a slow-but-live token holder's delayed handoff never causes a lost or clobbered update.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od9m2p3t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Slots, Feeders, NoSlot

VARIABLES held, phase, pendingSlot, votes

vars == <<held, phase, pendingSlot, votes>>

\* held[f] is feeder f's own local view of the slots it currently owns.
\* phase/pendingSlot/votes model the 2PC handshake: a feeder must prepare
\* (lock intent, recorded in votes) before it may commit a slot into held.
\* AdminOverride is the escape hatch that skips the handshake but still
\* moves ownership atomically, so it can never create a second holder.

TypeOK ==
  /\ held \in [Feeders -> SUBSET Slots]
  /\ phase \in [Feeders -> {"idle", "prepared"}]
  /\ pendingSlot \in [Feeders -> Slots \cup {NoSlot}]
  /\ votes \in [Slots -> SUBSET Feeders]

Init ==
  /\ held = [f \in Feeders |-> {}]
  /\ phase = [f \in Feeders |-> "idle"]
  /\ pendingSlot = [f \in Feeders |-> NoSlot]
  /\ votes = [s \in Slots |-> {}]

HeldBy(s) == {f \in Feeders : s \in held[f]}

Prepare(f, s) ==
  /\ phase[f] = "idle"
  /\ votes[s] = {}
  /\ HeldBy(s) = {}
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![f] = "prepared"]
  /\ pendingSlot' = [pendingSlot EXCEPT ![f] = s]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = {f}]
  /\ UNCHANGED held

Commit(f) ==
  /\ phase[f] = "prepared"
  /\ LET s == pendingSlot[f] IN
       /\ votes[s] = {f}
       /\ HeldBy(s) = {}
       /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![f] = held[f] \cup {s}]
       /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = {}]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![f] = "idle"]
  /\ pendingSlot' = [pendingSlot EXCEPT ![f] = NoSlot]

Abort(f) ==
  /\ phase[f] = "prepared"
  /\ LET s == pendingSlot[f] IN
       votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = @ \ {f}]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![f] = "idle"]
  /\ pendingSlot' = [pendingSlot EXCEPT ![f] = NoSlot]
  /\ UNCHANGED held

Release(f, s) ==
  /\ s \in held[f]
  /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![f] = @ \ {s}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, pendingSlot, votes>>

\* Emergency override: the operator forces slot s onto newf right now.
\* Every feeder's held set is updated in one step so the old holder (if
\* any) loses the slot at the same instant the new holder gains it.
AdminOverride(s, newf) ==
  /\ newf \in Feeders
  /\ held' = [g \in Feeders |-> IF g = newf THEN held[g] \cup {s} ELSE held[g] \ {s}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, pendingSlot, votes>>

Next ==
  \/ \E f \in Feeders, s \in Slots : Prepare(f, s)
  \/ \E f \in Feeders : Commit(f)
  \/ \E f \in Feeders : Abort(f)
  \/ \E f \in Feeders, s \in Slots : Release(f, s)
  \/ \E s \in Slots, newf \in Feeders : AdminOverride(s, newf)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Cross-feeder claim: a slot's set of holders never exceeds size one,
\* whether ownership moved via 2PC commit or via the admin override.
NoDoubleAllocation == \A s \in Slots : Cardinality(HeldBy(s)) <= 1

====
nl: A power-grid load shedder manages a fixed pool of shed-capacity slots that cap how much load each feeder is allowed to shed during peak stress. Feeders acquire a slot through a two-phase commit protocol: a feeder first prepares by locking its intent on a specific slot that no one else is holding or has an outstanding prepare on, and it may only commit that slot into its own held set once it is confirmed as the sole preparer and the slot is still unheld by anyone. A feeder may instead abort a prepared request without ever taking the slot, or release a slot it currently holds back to the free pool for others to acquire later. Separately, a privileged grid operator can invoke an emergency admin override that reassigns a slot directly from whoever currently holds it to a different feeder, completely bypassing the ordinary prepare/commit handshake, but the reassignment always moves the slot atomically to the new feeder rather than granting it to a second feeder while the first still holds it. The system must guarantee, across every feeder's local view, that no slot is ever simultaneously believed to be held by two different feeders, whether that state arose from the normal two-phase commit handshake among feeders or from the admin override forcing an emergency reassignment. SAFETY PROPERTY: No shed-capacity slot is ever held by more than one feeder at the same time, even after a privileged admin override forces an emergency reassignment.

spec_text:
------------------------------ MODULE W4Od17m4p5t4 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS
    Bags,       \* the finite set of bag identifiers handled by the router
    MinCap,     \* smallest allowed queue capacity bound
    MaxCap      \* largest allowed queue capacity bound

ASSUME MinCap \in Nat /\ MaxCap \in Nat
ASSUME 1 <= MinCap /\ MinCap <= MaxCap

\* pending: not-yet-queued bags. queue: FIFO awaiting dispatch. capacity:
\* live-resizable bound. dispatched/dispatchCount: irreversible-dispatch record.
VARIABLES pending, queue, capacity, dispatched, dispatchCount

vars == <<pending, queue, capacity, dispatched, dispatchCount>>

\* Mechanism: bounded FIFO queue with backpressure. Enqueue is only enabled
\* below the current capacity bound; Dispatch (the irreversible action) is
\* independent of capacity, so a live resize can never trap a queued bag.

CapRange == MinCap..MaxCap

BagInQueue(b) == \E i \in DOMAIN queue : queue[i] = b

TypeOK == /\ pending \subseteq Bags
          /\ queue \in Seq(Bags)
          /\ capacity \in CapRange
          /\ dispatched \subseteq Bags
          /\ dispatchCount \in [Bags -> Nat]

Init == /\ pending = Bags
        /\ queue = <<>>
        /\ capacity = MinCap
        /\ dispatched = {}
        /\ dispatchCount = [b \in Bags |-> 0]

Enqueue(b) == /\ b \in pending
              /\ Len(queue) < capacity
              /\ queue' = Append(queue, b)
              /\ pending' = pending \ {b}
              /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, dispatched, dispatchCount>>

\* Dispatch is the irreversible carousel drop-off: it removes the head bag,
\* records it as dispatched, and bumps its counter. It never reads capacity.
Dispatch == /\ queue # <<>>
            /\ LET b == Head(queue) IN
                 /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
                 /\ dispatched' = dispatched \cup {b}
                 /\ dispatchCount' = [dispatchCount EXCEPT ![b] = @ + 1]
            /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, capacity>>

Grow == /\ capacity < MaxCap
        /\ capacity' = capacity + 1
        /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, queue, dispatched, dispatchCount>>

Shrink == /\ capacity > MinCap
          /\ capacity' = capacity - 1
          /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, queue, dispatched, dispatchCount>>

EnqueueStep == \E b \in Bags : Enqueue(b)

Next == EnqueueStep \/ Dispatch \/ Grow \/ Shrink

\* Fairness: Dispatch and Enqueue must each make progress whenever they stay
\* enabled, so resizing capacity can only delay, never permanently block, a
\* queued bag's trip to the carousel.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Dispatch) /\ WF_vars(EnqueueStep)

\* Safety: a bag is never dispatched twice, and the queue never holds the
\* same bag in two slots at once (either would signal a duplicate dispatch).
OnlyOnceEver == /\ \A b \in Bags : dispatchCount[b] <= 1
                /\ \A i \in DOMAIN queue : \A j \in DOMAIN queue :
                       i # j => queue[i] # queue[j]

\* Liveness: any bag that ever sits in the queue eventually reaches the
\* carousel, across arbitrarily many Grow/Shrink resizes along the way.
EventuallyDispatched == \A b \in Bags : (BagInQueue(b) ~> (b \in dispatched))

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    b1 = b1
    b2 = b2
    b3 = b3
    b4 = b4
    Bags = {b1, b2, b3, b4}
    MinCap = 1
    MaxCap = 3

INVARIANT OnlyOnceEver

PROPERTY EventuallyDispatched
nl:
An airport baggage router accepts bags waiting to be sorted and holds them in a single FIFO work queue before they are dropped onto a carousel. The queue is bounded by a capacity limit that operations staff can raise or lower at any time in response to conveyor load, so a bag can only be enqueued while the queue has room under the current bound (backpressure). Four actions drive the system: Enqueue moves a waiting bag into the queue if it is not already full; Dispatch removes the bag at the head of the queue and irreversibly drops it onto the carousel, an action that can never be undone or repeated for that bag; Grow raises the capacity bound up to a configured maximum; and Shrink lowers the capacity bound down to a configured minimum, even while bags remain queued. Because dispatch never checks the capacity bound, resizing the queue can never prevent an already-queued bag from eventually reaching the carousel.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No bag is ever counted as dispatched to the carousel more than once, and the queue never holds the same bag in two positions at once.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every bag enqueued for final routing is eventually irreversibly dispatched to a carousel, regardless of how many times the capacity bound is grown or shrunk while it waits.

spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od19m9p3t0 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Patrons, Slots, Librarians, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES epoch, crashed, localEpoch, allocLog, pending

vars == <<epoch, crashed, localEpoch, allocLog, pending>>

\* Epoch-numbered reconfiguration: a librarian's writes only count once its
\* local epoch matches the current global one. A crashed node never syncs
\* again, so its stale belief is permanently fenced out of future grants.

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
  /\ crashed \subseteq Librarians
  /\ localEpoch \in [Librarians -> 0..MaxEpoch]
  /\ allocLog \subseteq [slot: Slots, pat: Patrons, ep: 0..MaxEpoch]
  /\ pending \subseteq (Patrons \times Slots)

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ crashed = {}
  /\ localEpoch = [l \in Librarians |-> 0]
  /\ allocLog = {}
  /\ pending = {}

RequestSlot(p, s) ==
  /\ ~ \E ss \in Slots : <<p, ss>> \in pending
  /\ pending' = pending \cup {<<p, s>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, crashed, localEpoch, allocLog>>

Crash(l) ==
  /\ crashed = {}                        \* twist: at most one crash, ever
  /\ crashed' = {l}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, localEpoch, allocLog, pending>>

Reconfigure ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ \E l \in Librarians \ crashed : TRUE   \* some live librarian survives
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, localEpoch, allocLog, pending>>

Sync(l) ==
  /\ l \notin crashed
  /\ localEpoch[l] < epoch
  /\ localEpoch' = [localEpoch EXCEPT ![l] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, crashed, allocLog, pending>>

Allocate(l, p, s) ==
  /\ l \notin crashed
  /\ localEpoch[l] = epoch
  /\ <<p, s>> \in pending
  /\ ~ \E r \in allocLog : r.slot = s
  /\ allocLog' = allocLog \cup {[slot |-> s, pat |-> p, ep |-> epoch]}
  /\ pending' = pending \ {<<p, s>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, crashed, localEpoch>>

Deny(l, p, s) ==
  /\ l \notin crashed
  /\ localEpoch[l] = epoch
  /\ <<p, s>> \in pending
  /\ \E r \in allocLog : r.slot = s
  /\ pending' = pending \ {<<p, s>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, crashed, localEpoch, allocLog>>

SyncAny == \E l \in Librarians : Sync(l)
ResolveReq(p, s) == \E l \in Librarians : Allocate(l, p, s) \/ Deny(l, p, s)

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Patrons, s \in Slots : RequestSlot(p, s)
  \/ \E l \in Librarians : Crash(l)
  \/ Reconfigure
  \/ SyncAny
  \/ \E p \in Patrons, s \in Slots : ResolveReq(p, s)

\* fairness is scoped to whichever librarians are still live: crashed
\* nodes can never satisfy Sync/Allocate/Deny's guards, so progress only
\* ever needs the surviving librarian. Fairness is per-request so one
\* patron's pending slot cannot starve forever behind another's traffic.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(SyncAny)
             /\ (\A p \in Patrons, s \in Slots : WF_vars(ResolveReq(p, s)))

\* invariant: two records for the same slot must agree on patron and epoch
NoDoubleAllocation ==
  \A r1, r2 \in allocLog :
    r1.slot = r2.slot => (r1.pat = r2.pat /\ r1.ep = r2.ep)

RequestsResolve ==
  \A p \in Patrons, s \in Slots : <<p, s>> \in pending ~> <<p, s>> \notin pending

=============================================================================
nl:
A small library runs a book-reservation service backed by a pool of librarian nodes that jointly track which physical copies (slots) are checked out. The service is organized into epochs: whenever the acting librarian is suspected to have failed, an epoch-numbered reconfiguration advances a global epoch counter, and only a librarian whose locally-known epoch matches the current one is allowed to grant or deny a reservation. Each patron keeps at most one outstanding request at a time for a copy; a live, epoch-synced librarian either allocates the copy to the requesting patron (recording both the patron and the epoch of the grant) if the copy is still unclaimed, or issues a definitive denial if the copy was already granted to someone. Exactly one librarian may crash silently at any point, permanently ceasing all activity, including any future re-synchronization to newer epochs, which fences its stale epoch belief out of all later decisions. Librarians resynchronize their own local epoch to the current global one whenever a reconfiguration has moved ahead of them. The full action set is: a patron requesting a copy, a librarian crashing, a reconfiguration advancing the epoch, a librarian resynchronizing its local epoch, a librarian allocating an unclaimed copy, and a librarian denying an already-granted copy.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No two allocation records ever name the same slot while disagreeing on which patron or which granting epoch it belongs to, so a given copy is never simultaneously granted to two different patrons.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every patron request for a copy is eventually resolved with either an allocation or a definitive denial, even though one librarian node may crash silently, because the epoch mechanism fences its stale authority out and leaves the remaining live librarian free to keep making progress.

---- MODULE W4Od2m8p2t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Robots, NoRobot, TotalUnits, MinCapacity, MaxCapacity

VARIABLES stock, payload, zoneLock, bayLock, capacity

vars == <<stock, payload, zoneLock, bayLock, capacity>>

\* Hierarchical locking: a robot must hold the coarse zoneLock before it can
\* take the finer bayLock on its own bay; locks release in reverse order.
\* capacity is a live-resizable ceiling on a bay's contents, changed only
\* when the whole fleet is unlocked so it never overlaps a load/unload.
RECURSIVE SumPayload(_, _)
SumPayload(f, S) ==
  IF S = {} THEN 0
  ELSE LET x == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE
       IN f[x] + SumPayload(f, S \ {x})

TypeOK == /\ stock \in 0..TotalUnits
          /\ payload \in [Robots -> 0..TotalUnits]
          /\ zoneLock \in Robots \cup {NoRobot}
          /\ bayLock \in Robots \cup {NoRobot}
          /\ capacity \in MinCapacity..MaxCapacity

Init == /\ stock = TotalUnits
        /\ payload = [r \in Robots |-> 0]
        /\ zoneLock = NoRobot
        /\ bayLock = NoRobot
        /\ capacity = MaxCapacity

AcquireZoneLock(r) ==
  /\ zoneLock = NoRobot
  /\ zoneLock' = r
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, payload, bayLock, capacity>>

AcquireBayLock(r) ==
  /\ zoneLock = r
  /\ bayLock = NoRobot
  /\ bayLock' = r
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, payload, zoneLock, capacity>>

LoadUnit(r) ==
  /\ bayLock = r
  /\ stock > 0
  /\ payload[r] < capacity
  /\ stock' = stock - 1
  /\ payload' = [payload EXCEPT ![r] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<zoneLock, bayLock, capacity>>

UnloadUnit(r) ==
  /\ bayLock = r
  /\ payload[r] > 0
  /\ stock' = stock + 1
  /\ payload' = [payload EXCEPT ![r] = @ - 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<zoneLock, bayLock, capacity>>

ReleaseBayLock(r) ==
  /\ bayLock = r
  /\ bayLock' = NoRobot
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, payload, zoneLock, capacity>>

ReleaseZoneLock(r) ==
  /\ zoneLock = r
  /\ bayLock = NoRobot
  /\ zoneLock' = NoRobot
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, payload, bayLock, capacity>>

ResizeCapacity ==
  /\ zoneLock = NoRobot
  /\ bayLock = NoRobot
  /\ \E newCap \in MinCapacity..MaxCapacity : capacity' = newCap
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, payload, zoneLock, bayLock>>

Next == \E r \in Robots :
          \/ AcquireZoneLock(r)
          \/ AcquireBayLock(r)
          \/ LoadUnit(r)
          \/ UnloadUnit(r)
          \/ ReleaseBayLock(r)
          \/ ReleaseZoneLock(r)
          \/ ResizeCapacity

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Conservation invariant: every unit is either in the shared pool or in
\* exactly one robot's bay; the grand total is unaffected by lock state
\* or by resizing the active capacity ceiling.
ConservationInvariant ==
  stock + SumPayload(payload, Robots) = TotalUnits
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

    Robots = {r1, r2, r3}
    NoRobot = NoRobot
    TotalUnits = 6
    MinCapacity = 2
    MaxCapacity = 4
INVARIANT ConservationInvariant
nl:
A fleet of warehouse robots shares a central stock pool of interchangeable units. To move a unit between the pool and its own payload bay, a robot must first acquire a coarse zone lock covering its work area, and then, only while holding that zone lock, acquire a finer per-bay lock on its own payload bay; both locks must later be released, bay lock first, in the reverse order they were taken. While holding its bay lock a robot may load one unit from the stock pool into its bay (if the bay has not reached the currently active capacity) or unload one unit from its bay back into the pool. Separately, fleet operations can resize the active bay capacity at any time, but only while no robot anywhere is holding a zone or bay lock, so a resize can never race with an in-progress load or unload. The full action set is: AcquireZoneLock, AcquireBayLock, LoadUnit, UnloadUnit, ReleaseBayLock, ReleaseZoneLock, and ResizeCapacity. Every unit in the system is always either resting in the shared stock pool or held in exactly one robot's payload bay, and the resize twist changes only how much a bay may hold going forward, never how many units currently exist.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The sum of units in the shared stock pool and units held across all robots' payload bays always equals the fixed grand total of units in the system, regardless of lock state or how the active bay capacity has been resized.
